summary: American Municipal Power answers the MISO abeyance motion, saying it falls short of the Show Cause Order's standards, and asks FERC to condition any abeyance on a cost-transparency and cost-shifting proposal within 20 days and a compliance filing by November 16.
ask: Direct MISO to present a cost-transparency and cost-shifting proposal within 20 days, vet it with states and customers, and file compliant Tariff revisions by November 16, 2026.

points.point: AMP says the motion fails the Show Cause Order's abeyance standards, so FERC has grounds to deny it.
points.quote: The Motion fails to provide the information required by the Commission’s June 18 Show Cause Order in the event abeyance is sought

points.point: AMP names the missing protections: disclosure of upgrades and costs, cost recovery agreements, financial security and stranded-cost protection.
points.quote: public disclosure of large-load-driven network upgrades and their costs, cost recovery agreements, financial security requirements, and protection of existing transmission customers from stranded costs

points.point: AMP calls MISO's roadmap a few lines with a vague November filing.
points.quote: This falls well short of the detailed roadmap to compliance that the Commission required to justify abeyance.

points.point: AMP says upgrade costs are likely in the billions and MISO has presented no cost proposals in the stakeholder process.
points.quote: Costs associated with transmission upgrades to serve large loads are likely to be in the billions of dollars.

points.point: AMP says municipal and cooperative transmission-dependent utilities are not protected by state commissions because zonal cost allocation is wholesale.
points.quote: Transmission dependent utilities such as municipalities and cooperatives are not protected by state utility commissions and retail tariffs

points.point: AMP proposes three directives to MISO.
points.quote: bring forward a specific proposal to meet its obligations under the Show Cause Order to address cost transparency and cost shifting within the next twenty days

throughLine.text: Opposes abeyance of the E-8 deadline unless MISO advances the order's cost-recovery agreement, financial security and cost-transparency directives; FERC granted abeyance but cited AMP's objection.
